 "Summary": "Fix the mixing proportion of the posterior-weighted MIL mixture to the witness rate estimated by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation, and fit only the lesion component, which makes the per-patch posteriors stable early in training while keeping soft targets.",
 "Hypothesis": "Anchoring the mixture proportion to the MPE estimate reduces the epoch-to-epoch variation of the fitted lesion posterior by at least 50% and raises held-out AUPRO by at least 1 point over free-proportion posterior MIL.",
 "Rationale": "The witness-rate parent estimates the proportion of lesion patches robustly but uses it only as a hard k; the posterior parent uses soft targets but must estimate proportion and lesion component jointly, which is unstable when the two distributions overlap early in training.  "Method": "1) Every 2 epochs per source dataset and level: pi_d from the best-bin MPE estimator; f0 from normal-image patch scores (kernel density); f1 Gaussian fitted by EM with pi fixed to pi_d. 2) Posterior weights as in posterior MIL; weighted BCE for abnormal images; BCE towards 0 for normal images. 3) First 2 epochs: top-k MIL.
